findings.condition: DRC with --severity-all reports 13 error-severity violations on the saved board: padstack x5, annular_width x5, starved_thermal x3 (by_type/by_severity in the drc check record; console confirms 142 total violations).

evidence.locator: by_type: padstack=5, annular_width=5, starved_thermal=3; by_severity: error=13 (summarized in drc check details; individual entries beyond byte 100000 of the excerpt)

findings.location: Polygonus-Universal-Base.kicad_pcb (specific items truncated out of supplied drc.json excerpt)
findings.mechanism: Annular ring below minimum risks drill breakout and open or intermittent plated-through connections after fabrication; padstack errors risk fab rejection or unreliable via construction; starved thermal reliefs mean pads join their copper zones through insufficient spokes, constricting the electrical connection and degrading solderability on what are typically ground/power pads.
findings.reasoning: These are native tool errors on the saved copper, not tool failures. The exact coordinates are not in the supplied excerpt, so the count and classification come from the tool's own summary; the physical failure modes they encode (drill breakout, starved zone connection) are manufacturing and connectivity risks independent of location. Zone-fill-as-saved is a caveat for the starved_thermal subset only.
findings.title: Saved board has 13 DRC error-severity violations: padstack, annular width, and starved thermal

findings.condition: The README states the two wideband controllers are connected internally to CAN bus #2. The CAN2+/CAN2- nets join U20.7/6, U21.7/6, J2.73/74, J1.15/11, protectors D10/D11 and filter caps, plus terminators R36.1/2 and R37.1/2. Both R36 and R37 are marked (dnp yes)(in_bom no) in the native sheet and dnp:true in the netlist, so the saved board ships with zero on-board CAN2 termination.

evidence.locator: symbol R36 (uuid d69380f9-5487-4782-9ce9-0690df62e543): value 120, (in_bom no)(dnp yes), instances R36/R37
nets /CAN2+ and /CAN2- include R36.1/R37.1 and R36.2/R37.2; components R36, R37 dnp:true
'Dual wideband O2 sensor controllers ... connected internally to CAN bus #2'

findings.location: wbo-can-trans.kicad_sch (R36 at 115.57,86.36, two sheet instances R36/R37); board: R36 at (175.01,140.67), R37 at (81.62,140.55)
findings.mechanism: U20 and U21 sit at roughly opposite board edges (R36 near x=175 mm, R37/U21 near x=75-82 mm), so the populated pair would form correct split end-termination. With both DNP, the internal multi-node bus between the two wideband MCUs, the ECU module, and the harness pins is unterminated unless the external harness supplies both 120 ohm ends; reflections on an unterminated or singly-terminated bus can corrupt wideband CAN traffic at typical 500 kbit rates.
findings.reasoning: Marked as a concern rather than a defect because the DNP may be a deliberate builder option (CAN2 is also exposed on J1 pins 11/15 for external nodes, where double internal termination would conflict with harness terminators). However, no documentation in the packet instructs the builder to terminate externally, and the advertised internal wideband function depends on a properly terminated bus, so the as-saved population is a real signal-integrity risk that the scope explicitly asks to be reviewed.
findings.title: Internal dual-wideband CAN2 bus has both 120 ohm terminators (R36, R37) unpopulated

findings.condition: ERC reports 5 errors: GND power input #PWR01 not driven (36.83,78.74); A1 pin 8 VMOT power input not driven (48.26,219.71); J2 pin 90 12V_IGN power input not driven (293.37,173.99); J2 pins 40/41 both Power-output type tied together on 5V_SENSOR_1 (262.89,128.27/130.81); A1 pin 2 ~FLT output unconnected with no no-connect marker (38.1,224.79).

evidence.locator: root sheet '/': power_pin_not_driven x3 (uuids ad746bdd, acdd6b6d, 3d2dd476), pin_to_pin (2f453565/b5fc1cf2), pin_not_connected A1 pin 2 (a25f94e0)

findings.mechanism: The undriven power-input errors indicate battery/harness-fed nets (12V_KEY, VMOT via 12V_MR_FUSE) and GND lack PWR_FLAG markers, so the tool cannot confirm a power source; the pin_to_pin error is two power-output pins of the same module symbol paralleled; the unconnected DRV8825 ~FLT pin means stepper-driver fault reporting is physically unmonitored and the omission is unmarked, so it cannot be distinguished from an accidental open.
findings.reasoning: These are confirmed native errors. Electrically, the undriven-power and paralleled-output cases are explainable (harness-fed rails, duplicated module pins) and therefore minor, but they remain unresolved errors that mask any future genuine power-sourcing fault; the unmarked ~FLT open is a small functional gap (no stepper fault detection) rather than a hazard.
findings.title: Five ERC error-severity violations: undriven power inputs, power-output conflict, unconnected fault pin

findings.condition: Schematic parity reports: 'Simon:Polygonus-With-USB-SWD doesn't match footprint given by symbol (fome_modules:polygonus)' plus an exclude-from-BOM attribute mismatch for footprint J2.

evidence.locator: schematic_parity entries for 'Footprint J2' (uuid f447e585-df78-4239-b8cb-4653b3837bb1), types footprint_symbol_mismatch

findings.mechanism: The board carries a different footprint variant for the central ECU brain-module connector than the schematic assigns. Net-level parity passed (0 unconnected items), so pad-to-net mapping currently agrees, but the divergent footprint identity means mechanical outline, extra pads (USB/SWD variant), or future re-sync from schematic could silently alter the board, and the Simon library is absent from the verification environment so the placed footprint could not be validated against any source.
findings.reasoning: Concern rather than defect: connectivity parity holds and the substitution is plausibly an intentional variant with USB/SWD breakout, but the schematic/board divergence on the single most connected component (107 pins) is a configuration-management risk, especially with the source library unavailable for comparison.
findings.title: Main module footprint on board differs from schematic assignment (J2)

evidence.locator: components C23-C25, R25-R34, U10, JP1 on sheet /VR Conditioner/ (uuid 76f66c7e-94ea-4f9a-aa2e-a01725934e38)

findings.mechanism: Two byte-identical files with case-differing names coexist in the project. On case-insensitive filesystems they collide; on case-sensitive systems future edits can land in whichever copy a given tool resolves, silently forking the VR conditioner sheet (MAX9924 crank input chain, C23-C25, R25-R34, JP1). All connectivity verified here is against the alias, not the original file path.
findings.reasoning: The alias is explicitly declared as a disposable workaround, so this is not a new defect, but the physical design content of the VR conditioner now has two potential sources of truth; the verified netlist applies only to the alias as supplied.
findings.title: Hierarchy depends on disposable 'VR Conditioner.kicad_sch' byte-copy alias of the lowercase original

findings.condition: Nets /CAN+ (J1.47, J2.93) and /CAN- (J1.46, J2.94) run directly from the harness connector to the brain-module connector with no TVS, filter capacitors, or termination footprints on the base board, whereas CAN2 carries NUP2105L protectors (D10/D11), 47 pF filters, and terminator footprints.
findings.mechanism: If the Polygonus module does not include transceiver-side protection, the primary vehicle CAN lines enter the module unprotected against harness ESD/transients; the asymmetry versus CAN2 suggests protection was assumed to live on the module, which cannot be confirmed from this packet.
findings.reasoning: No requirement for base-board CAN1 protection is declared, and the module (out of scope) plausibly provides it, so this is recorded only as an informational observation about the asymmetric protection scheme and the coverage boundary, not as a fault.
findings.title: Main CAN bus (CAN1) has no board-level ESD protection or filtering, unlike CAN2

limitations: Several artifacts were truncated in the packet: drc.json (100000/142607 bytes, the 13 error-severity entries for padstack/annular_width/starved_thermal are not visible), erc.json (100000/226344), geometry.json (100000/1657568, tracks/vias/zones not included), design.xml (84913/252017); geometry execution.json and console.log were omitted entirely. Error locations for the DRC errors are therefore known only by count and type.

No trace width, copper ampacity, thermal, or return-path evaluation was possible: the geometry excerpt contains only footprint/pad data, no track or zone geometry, and no current requirements were declared. Per instructions, no ampacity or thermal qualification is inferred.
Zone fill was evaluated as saved; the read-only candidate forbids a refill, so the 3 starved_thermal errors reflect the saved fill state and could change after a refill.

The verification environment lacks the project libraries Simon, hellen-one-common, fome_modules and header_placement, so ~200 lib_symbol/lib_footprint mismatch or issue warnings could not be resolved against library sources; cached symbols/footprints were accepted as-is.
External harness behavior (CAN bus length, external termination, ignition transients, EMC) is out of scope per the declared limitations and was not assessed.
The Polygonus brain module (J2) internals are not part of this donor packet, so protection/termination possibly located on the module (e.g., for CAN1) could not be verified.
